title: Per-tenant prefix amortizer with asymmetric late-arrival adjustment
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Late-arriving token events (out-of-order ingestion from edge proxies and retries) cause tenant-level cost volatility and occasional negative invoices after retroactive credits. Current windowed amortizers apply symmetric refunds which over-correct multi-route sessions and penalize bursty tenants.

Goal: Implement a per-tenant prefix amortizer that attributes late-arriving tokens proportionally to recent session prefixes with an asymmetric adjustment rule to avoid over-refunding. The component should run as a fault-tolerant job in the metering pipeline, emit explainable attribution decisions, and support configurable confidence thresholds for auto-applied corrections vs. manual review.
acceptance_criteria:
- New amortizer job produces deterministic allocations for synthetic late-arrival scenarios in the test harness (unit + integration).
- End-to-end pipeline preserves idempotency: replays of the same late events do not change final tenant cost beyond tolerance.
- Console shows per-tenant amortization events with rationale and confidence score in the billing timeline.
- Nightly backfill reduces historical negative-adjustment incidents by >= 90% on the sample customers without increasing false-positive refunds by > 5%.
- Feature flag gated rollout and canary to 5% of tenants with automatic rollback on SLO/regression alerts.
design_notes:
High level approach:
1) For each late token event, compute a prefix affinity vector using recent session affinity (last 24h, decayed). Prefixes are derived from model route + prompt fingerprint + session tag.
2) Score candidate prefixes by temporal proximity and token weight; normalize to tenant-level allocation.
3) Apply asymmetric adjustment: when a refund reduces a tenant's net charge below zero within a sliding window, cap refund at a configurable floor and mark remainder for manual adjudication.
4) Emit audit records containing original event id, candidate prefix weights, chosen allocation, confidence, and causation tags for upstream reconciler and billing UI.

Schema changes: add amortizer_event table columns: event_id, tenant_id, allocated_prefixes (encoded list), allocation_weights (encoded list), confidence_score, adjudication_state. Use existing provenance_id to link to token ledger entries.

Throughput: job should scale horizontally; target processing latency for backlog batches is <= 30s per batch of 10k events.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2w): design proto and offline scorer; unit tests with synthetic replay harness.
Phase 2 (2w): implement streaming amortizer worker using existing metering-worker framework; add telemetry and audit emission.
Phase 3 (1w): console integration (billing timeline rows + link to audit record); add permissioned manual adjudication UI placeholder.
Phase 4 (1w): canary rollout behind feature flag; run backfill job for 30-day window; monitor metrics and iterate.

Key tasks:
- Create amortizer schema migration and idempotent upsert job.
- Implement scorer with pluggable decay function.
- Integrate with ledger-merge worker for safe credit application.
- Add policy to cap auto-refunds and enqueue manual tickets for adjudication.
- End-to-end tests and synthetic fault injection (out-of-order, duplicate events, partial failures).
migration_steps:
1) Deploy schema migration in readonly mode; validate schema.
2) Run dry-run amortizer on a shadow dataset to collect allocations without touching accounts.
3) Compare dry-run vs. current manual corrections to tune thresholds.
4) Enable feature-flagged write path for 5% of tenants; run canary and monitor.
5) Gradually increase to 100% and trigger backfill for historical window.
6) After validation, retire legacy symmetric amortization job.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Metrics to emit: amortizer.processed_events, amortizer.allocations_ratio, amortizer.avg_latency_ms, amortizer.confidence_histogram, amortizer.auto_refund_count, amortizer.manual_enqueue_count.
Alerts:
- SLO breach if avg_latency_ms > 2000ms for 5m.
- Spike in manual_enqueue_count > 3x baseline for 15m.
- Net negative-credits post-backfill increase > 1% triggers rollback.
- Audit emission failures > 0.1% of processed events for 10m.
Dashboards: per-region and per-tenant heatmap for refunded amounts and enqueued adjudications.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Incorrect prefix scoring could misallocate cost, impacting revenue. Mitigation: start with conservative confidence threshold and shadow runs; run offline validation against labeled incidents.
Risk: Backfill could create large retroactive refunds. Mitigation: cap backfill exposure per-tenant and add manual approval step for high-value adjustments.
Risk: Increased storage for amortizer audit records. Mitigation: TTL policy and compressed encoding; roll to cold storage after retention window.
Risk: Race with concurrent ledger reconciliation jobs. Mitigation: acquire lightweight fencing token per-tenant and write idempotent ledger ops.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for scorer and asymmetric cap logic.
- Integration tests: replay harness with permutations of out-of-order, duplicates, and delayed events.
- Load test: simulate production ingestion rates (10k events/sec) in a staging cluster to validate horizontal scaling.
- Regression suite: compare before/after snapshots of billing for a representative tenant cohort.
- Security review: ensure audit payloads do not expose PII; run SAST for new endpoints.
rollout_and_rollback:
Rollout strategy: feature flag + staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) over 2 weeks.
Rollback plan: flip feature flag to shadow mode, run compensating job to revert last canary writes (idempotent), and pause backfill. Document rollback playbook and contact list.
Postmortem: if >3 customers impacted or >$10k unexpected refunds, require SR and full postmortem within 7 days.
